The red is a CI failure. Deleting the skeleton is not available: it is the declared Replacement, and removing it raises change.superseded-replacement-not-found.
Three decisions this spec makes, because the work already exists:
1. Execution means verify and close, not build. Gates still require a plan and a review verdict, so this bundle will be executed. Target assertions are already true at the start. That is acceptable. A BaselineAssertions block that describes the pre-2b35230 tree (MustContain the old "expected while a C-* change is in progress" phrase) would be false today and would look like real baseline breakage. Do not author that baseline. Do not revert production files to manufacture a red. BaselineAssertions of the later plan describe the already-present implementation and are expected to pass at plan approval.
2. A ratification asserts two distinct claims, both required. "The code is unchanged by this bundle" is AC-NO-PRODUCTION-WRITE. "The code is still correct" is the predecessor feature criteria, re-verified by the same tests, already green. Either claim alone is insufficient: unchanged bytes could ratify a later regression; correctness-only invites an executor to "fix" and rewrite. Byte-identity of all 18 ratified files to 2b35230 is not the unchanged claim — seven of them have legitimate later edits.
3. This bundle's production write surface is empty. The 18 production files 2b35230 changed are the ratified surface: already committed, this bundle does not edit them. The only files this bundle may write are this spec.xml and the later plan.xml. Derived from git show --name-only 2b35230 on 2026-09-02, not from the predecessor's ObservedWriteScope (which is the defect F133 named).

Goals.Goal: Attach valid governance to the already-committed C-LINT-PHASE-HONESTY implementation without rewriting it. This spec is the replacement named by the archived predecessor. Execution of this bundle verifies that the properties below still hold and closes the skeleton that F135 left load-bearing and red. It does not re-implement the feature.

Keep the honest current-mode lead line already in formatTextReport at src/lint/core.ts:780-787 (HEAD df8e366). When current mode reports N>0 semantically-evaluated BaselineAssertions issues, the text report still leads with one line and those issues remain severity error. Exact operator-facing text, singular N=1: Baseline assertion failures: 1. Current mode cannot tell whether writes have started. If the baseline is still the intended state, this is real breakage. If writes have started, use --assertions target --change C-ID. Plural N>1 uses "failures: N" and "these are real breakage". N=0 is unchanged: first line is neo-grace Lint Report. The lead line must not contain "expected" or "in progress" and must not name --assertions final. JSON.stringify of the result gains no new top-level key (D13).

Keep current as the default assertion mode at src/grace-lint.ts resolveAssertionMode:87. Keep evaluating approved-plan BaselineAssertions in current mode (src/lint/core.ts:519 evaluateCurrentBaseline). That predicate is evaluation, not an in-progress claim. Do not skip it. Do not infer writes-started from git dirty, the ledger, or ObservedWriteScope. This retains AC-BASELINE-LINT-FRAMING's evaluation half (C-REPORT-HONESTY / P0.9); it does not silently contradict that ruling.

Keep selected --assertions target without --run-commands an explicitly-structural query. shouldFail at src/grace-lint.ts:137-149 computes the default --fail-on errors gate over non-exempt error-severity issues. The exempt set is assertion.command-not-evaluated when result.assertionMode is target and result.commandsEnabled is false; otherwise empty. A coexisting non-exempt error still fails the exit. finalizeResult at src/lint/core.ts:251-256 stays a pure severity count. formatTextReport at src/lint/core.ts:811-817 prints the structural-query note. Exact singular N=1: 1 command assertion not evaluated; it does not fail this structural target query.

Keep validateAssertionPhase (src/artifact/assertions.ts:291-311) firing assertion.phase-incompatible-command on a TargetAssertions MustPassCommand whose command text is current-mode lint of this project root, whether --assertions current is explicit or omitted. Matcher is command text only, after flattening whitespace. Never read package.json and never resolve bun run <script> into script bodies. Archived plans stay exempt because isArchivedPlanFile (src/artifact/assertions.ts:287-298) returns no issues before the matcher runs; skipActivePhaseIssues at src/lint/core.ts:574 remains a second filter. That is the F133(b) shipped layer, not the predecessor spec's skipActivePhaseIssues-only location.

Keep the MustPassCommand doctrine, already rewritten across the ten surfaces, as this property: MustPassCommand contains leaf project evidence such as tests, typecheck, build, format, or package checks. Do not put a current-mode lint of this project root in TargetAssertions. Current mode means the command text contains --assertions current, or it invokes ngrace lint and omits --assertions. The restriction matches command text; it does not resolve bun run <script> through package.json, and it does not apply to --help or to lint of a different project root. Use selected target/final lint externally instead. README.md carries that paragraph at line 214 (HEAD df8e366). examples/cli/README.md carries it at line 21, including the structural-query sentence. This is a real README.md and examples/ decision: those two files were rewritten by 2b35230 as teaching surface for the doctrine, and this bundle keeps that teaching in place rather than reverting or restating it elsewhere.

Keep the structural-query property on the surfaces that already describe selected target without --run-commands. README.md CLI Overview target row (line 168 at HEAD df8e366) already uses optional [--run-commands] and names the query. examples/cli/README.md:16 already shows the without-flag invocation beside the --run-commands line.

Given an active approved plan whose BaselineAssertions include a failing MustNotExist (the C-REPORT-HONESTY fixture shape) and default text lint output, formatTextReport leads with Baseline assertion failures: 1.
